# Climb batch 25's probes

The runs were in three worktrees seeded detached at `dc571c1f3` from the base build `/home/user/fortress-base25`, whose code is `25238e60c`'s, after its build, library order and walk run had ended at 00:41 UTC on 2026-11-02 and before its marker `tmp/BUILT` was written at 01:28: `/home/user/fortress-p25` (the code generator's runs, then the samples of N, D and P with the `asFloat` control), `/home/user/fortress-p25t` (the texts of R, U and A, then the order of application) and `/home/user/fortress-p25patch` (the six texts and samples together, built). Each was removed after. The base build ran nothing but `old-fortress.sh` runs, with their private caches folders in the probe worktrees. Machine: nproc 4, Intel Xeon Processor @ 2.10 GHz, openjdk 25.0.4.1, `FORTRESS_THREADS=1` for the stages and the direct runs; two other workers shared the machine, the load from 0.3 to 5, so no time here is one to compare, and walk was not timed.

## The files

- `count.sh`: F-32's classes counted again on a built tree, made from `plan-24/probes/count.sh`: the natives probe's scripts read from `4a46fb83a`, with `plan-24/probes/remap.py` run on climb batch 24's table of its base, so that each of the 173 bindings that name a helper gets the glue class it named before it moved; then `plan-23/probes/movable.py`, then the column `now`. Writes `classified.tsv`, `movable.tsv`, `moved.tsv` and `helpers-javap.txt`; it reads the tree and builds nothing, so it was run on the base build itself.
- `classified-base.tsv`, `moved-base.tsv`: `count.sh`'s output on the base build. The first equals climb batch 24's `plan-24/probes/classified-base.tsv` binding for binding, line numbers included; the second lists the 173 bindings that name helpers, each with the glue class it named before it moved. Rungs A and U change six `asFloat` headers, from `Float` to `RR64`, so the next planner's `remap.py`, which matches by file, owner and header, must match those six by file and line, which their one-line edits keep.
- `n3.py` and `n3-base.tsv`: N3's 158, the class C bindings of `classified.tsv`, one line a binding with its line, owner, header, glue class, the batch's rung or the home of what it waits on, the helper's Java signature, the types the compiled checker reads it at in walk's world, whether microGPT's lines reach it, and the glue class's computation read from `interpreter/glue/prim/`. Its last lines, on standard error, count each rung.
- `codegen.sh` and `cgkinds.py`: the code generator over the distance stage's fourteen components, declaration by declaration, on the tree at `$FORTRESS_HOME`: the distance stage's shadows and driver (`tools/distance/`) with `-order full` and the flags of the probe of 2026-10-23 (`perf-probes/codegen-distance/REPORT.md`, section 1), whose own scripts were not kept. `cgkinds.py` counts each refused declaration once, at its first wall, by component and by the code generator's message. About 140 s on the base, 210 s with the helper strings on glue classes.
- `apply25.py`: writes a rung's text, or the planner's sample of one, into a tree at the base, by exact text, each edit matching once: `R`, `U` and `A` the whole texts; `N`, `D` and `P` the samples; `asfloat-control` `Int`'s `asFloat` moved at its header `Float`.
- `rung-R.patch`, `rung-U.patch`, `rung-A.patch`: `apply25.py`'s three texts on a clean checkout of the base, taken with `git diff`. `sample-D.patch`, `sample-P.patch`, `sample-N.patch`: its three samples, likewise. Each applies to the base alone (`git apply --check`), and the six one after another in the gather's order D, P, A, R, U, N through `git apply --3way`.

## How to run them again

From a worktree seeded from a base build at the batch's base, set up as the `fortress-repo` skill's `build-and-caches.md` says:

    explorations/compile-ladder/plan-25/probes/count.sh $PWD tmp/count
    python3 -B explorations/compile-ladder/plan-25/probes/n3.py tmp/count/classified.tsv ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/glue/prim > tmp/n3.tsv
    explorations/compile-ladder/plan-25/probes/codegen.sh tmp/cg                     # in the background; prints the table
    python3 -B explorations/compile-ladder/plan-25/probes/apply25.py $PWD R U A      # or: git apply --3way the patches in the gather's order
    ant compileAll        # then the library order, before a compiled test
    explorations/coordinator/tools/distance/run.sh tmp/distance.txt tmp/distance        # in the background
    explorations/coordinator/tools/checker-count/run.sh tmp/count.txt tmp/count-scratch # in the background
    ant testSystem; ant testSpecData                                                   # in the background

The control of the code generator's run puts the 173 helper strings back on their glue classes for one run, from `tmp/count/moved.tsv` (`glue_before`, `helper_now`), the string searched from the header's line through three lines after it, since a header can span two lines. The `asFloat` control is `apply25.py <tree> asfloat-control` with the distance stage after it.

The value probes were scratch programs, not kept, each run on the old code (`tools/old-fortress.sh /home/user/fortress-base25 <tree>/tmp/old-caches P.fss`) and on the text (`bin/fortress P.fss`), their outputs compared with `diff`: `ValR`, R's ten at the bounds and at pairs of signs; `ValU`, `UnsignedLong`'s getters and `NN64`'s prefix `DOTMINUS` at seven values, and `NN32`'s `CHOOSE` at 128 pairs, each overflow caught; `ValA`, the six `asFloat`s at their bounds; `ValN`, `ValD` and `ValQ`, the samples of N, D and P; `ZeroZZ32`, `ZeroZZ64`, `ZeroNN32`, `ZeroNN64` and `ZeroZZ`, `REM` and `MOD` by zero in a `try` catching `DivisionByZero`. Each was a do-block of typed bindings and `println` lines, written by a script: a list literal at a declared `List[\ZZ32\]` is an `ArrayList[\Int\]` under walk and does not bind (row 364's kind), so the lists were left out. The compiled sample, `SampleRUACompiled` and `SampleNDQCompiled`, each with a `.test` of `link`, `run` and `run_out_contains=PASS`, ran through `ONE_JVM=1 explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-N/merged-tests/junit.sh samples ProjectFortress/compiler_tests SampleRUACompiled.test SampleNDQCompiled.test` after the library order on the combined tree, and on the old code through `old-fortress.sh <base build> <caches> junit <the two .test files>`; the compiled prelude's `assert` has no form over two `ZZ64` values, so those comparisons are `assert(a = b, message)`.

native component Writer
import FlatString.FlatString
import Stream.{...}
export Writer

private language="java"
private package="com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.prim"

stdOut: Writer = OutWriter()
stdErr: Writer = ErrWriter()

private OutWriter(): Writer =  builtinPrimitive(
        "com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.prim.Writer$outputWriter")
private ErrWriter(): Writer = builtinPrimitive(
        "com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.prim.Writer$errorWriter")

object Writer(fileName: String) extends { WriteStream }
    getter asString(): String = "Writer on " self.fileName.asExprString
    getter fileName(): String =
      builtinPrimitive(
        "com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.prim.Writer$fileName")
    write(s:FlatString):() =
      builtinPrimitive(
        "com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.prim.Writer$write")
    write(c:Char):() =
      builtinPrimitive(
        "com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.prim.Writer$write")
    flush():() =
      builtinPrimitive(
        "com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.prim.Writer$flush")
    close():() =
      builtinPrimitive(
        "com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.prim.Writer$close")
    write(s: String): () = do
        buff = BufferedWriter(self, |s|)
        s.writeOn(buff)
        buff.flush()
    end
end Writer

object BufferedWriter(under: WriteStream, size: ZZ32) extends { WriteStream }
    getter asString(): String = "BufferedWriter on " under.asString
    write(s: String): () = s.writeOn(self)

## 1. The shape probe

### What was on record, and what is new

The 2026-09-20 probe ran five one-declaration programs and found four gaps, all in walk's half (`import-java-interpreter.md:88-228`). It did not change Java, so it could not see past the first gap each program met. New here: one component with two declarations bound through `import java`, in `CompilerBuiltin.fss`'s shape, one `import java` line per helper class, from one package (`natives-shape/NativesShape.fss`); a variant with both helpers in one line (`NativesShapeOne.fss`); and each gap patched in a shadow, one at a time, in the order a program meets them.

The helpers are `simpleIntArith.intLT(int,int):boolean` and `simpleDoubleArith.doubleAdd(double,double):double`. The compiled path runs both programs today and prints `true`, `false`, `5.5` (`natives-shape/03-compile-control.out`).

### What each gap does to it

1. **The type table.** On the unchanged tree both programs stop in name resolution: `FortressBuiltin.JavaString`, `RR64`, `ZZ32`, `ZZ64` are undefined (`01-NativesShape-walk.out`). `ForeignJava` synthesizes an api for every method of each helper class, and `NamingCzar`'s table places every Java type in the builtin api (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/NamingCzar.java:294-295`, `:436-450`). The one library places the number traits and `String` in `FortressLibrary` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:291`, `:513`, `:558`, `:2342`). Patch: in walk's world the table names the one library's types (`patches/gap1-namingczar-table.patch`, +14 −11). Then the two-line program meets gap 2 and the one-line program meets gap 3 (`04-*-g1.out`).
2. **The second import from one package.** `ClassCastException` at `Driver.java:466` (`04-NativesShape-g1.out`). The two callers that reach a foreign api do not read the value (`Driver.java:405`, `:410`). Patch: return `null` for a foreign wrapper (`gap2-driver-cast.patch`, +2 −2). Then gap 3 (`05-NativesShape-g12.out`).
3. **The foreign name.** "Non-top-level reference to imported …intLT" (`05-NativesShape-g12.out`), raised at `interpreter/evaluator/BaseEnv.java:535-537`. Walk's desugarer gives a reference its depth only when a rewrite matches its name (`interpreter/rewrite/DesugarerVisitor.java:668-681`); a foreign name has none, so it keeps the unset depth. The same visitor already sets an api-qualified type name to the top level (`:694-697`). Patch: the same for an api-qualified reference (`gap3-desugarer-qualified-ref.patch`, +3). The 2026-09-20 reading, that `ForeignComponentWrapper`'s empty rewrite map had to be filled (`import-java-interpreter.md:164-176`), was not needed. Then gap 4: a `NullPointerException` in `NativeApp.stringName` (`06-NativesShape-g123.out`).
4. **The closure.** `ClosureMaker` emits a class that calls the compiler's wrapper in `nativewrapper_cache`, which walk's classpath lacks, over an all-`FValue` descriptor (`import-java-interpreter.md:178-223`). Patch: a closure that calls the helper itself by reflection, unboxing each argument and boxing the result by its Java type (`gap4-reflective-closure.patch`, +71 −6: the new `interpreter/glue/ForeignNativeApp.java`, and the body of `ClosureMaker.closureForTopLevelFunction`, `ClosureMaker.java:119-141`, replaced). Then the closure has no parameter types (`NonPrimitive.java:309`, `07-NativesShape-g1234.out`), because `FunctionClosure.finishInitializing` (`FunctionClosure.java:232`) never runs on a foreign closure. Patch: the wrapper keeps its closures and finishes them after the libraries' types exist, from a pass after `initTypes` (`Driver.java:223-225`; `gap4b-foreign-closure-params.patch`, +17 −1). Both programs then print `true`, `false`, `5.5` on walk (`08-*-g1234b.out`).
5. **New: a helper that raises.** A helper raises a Fortress exception by naming a class of the compiled prelude, for example `Utility.makeFortressException("fortress.CompilerBuiltin$IntegerOverflow")` (`compiler/runtimeValues/Utility.java:45-58`); the helpers do so at 55 sites (IntegerOverflow 37, DivisionByZero 16, FileNotFoundException 2). Walk has no such class, so an overflow ends the run with `FortressImplementationError` (`13-NativesShapeRaise.out`). Patch: translate it into walk's own raise of the library object of that name, as `Int.overflow()` raises it (`interpreter/glue/prim/Int.java:258-261`; `gap5-helper-raise.patch`, +13). Then walk prints `IntegerOverflow caught`, as the compiled path does (`13-NativesShapeRaise.out`).

The same five patches run methods too: a trait's functional method and an object's dotted method whose bodies call the imported functions print `true`, `false`, `1.5` on walk and compiled (`NativesShapeMethod.fss`, `11-NativesShapeMethod.out`).

### What it costs and what it does not show

- **Size.** Six patches, +120 −20 lines of Java in six files, one of them new (`natives-shape/patches/`). Gap 1's patch is a probe device: at the switch-over the table names the one library's types for both paths, and the world test goes.
- **No regression.** The interpreter suite, what `ant testSystem` runs, in two shards: 441 tests green under the full shadow (`09-system-g12345.out`), as without it (`09-system-control.out`; the first control run was cut by the 14:35 UTC restart and re-run whole). The compiled path with the shadow first on the classpath compiles and runs `NativesShape` as before (`10-compile-under-shadow.out`). `testFast` was not run under the shadow.
- **Limits, by reading.** `ForeignNativeApp` converts `int`, `long`, `double`, `float`, `boolean`, `String` and `BigInteger`. Helpers over compiled-world types cannot take walk's values: 6 parameters or results over `fortress.AnyType$Any`, 13 over `fortress.CompilerBuiltin$IntLiteral`, 17 over `FortressBufferedReader`/`Writer`, 14 over `FZZ32Vector`/`FStringVector` (`natives-shape/helpers-javap.txt`). A shared text needs its helpers over Java values. `Char` carried as `int` and the unsigned types were not run. A reflective call is slower than a glue subclass; walk's speed was not measured.
- **The record's shape is not needed.** The 2026-09-20 note chose one api with a builtin component per path (`import-java-interpreter.md:43-47`). That shape needs the linker step of ledger row 320 (`linker/Linker.java:72-76`), and it does not reach the 125 bindings inside `FortressLibrary.fss` itself, nor those of `FlatString`, `Writer` and `NativeArray`.

### The library's own construct, walk's half

The one library binds every native with `builtinPrimitive("…")`. That construct can serve as the one text too, if its string names a static helper instead of a glue class. Walk's half measured: a 72-line loader (`patches/opt1-builtinprimitive-static.patch`, a fallback in `NativeApp.java:196` and the new `StaticNativeApp.java`, over `ForeignNativeApp`'s conversions) runs `builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleIntArith.intLT")` and prints `true`, `false`, `5.5` (`NativesShapeBP.fss`, `12-NativesShapeBP.out`); the unchanged tree refuses it ("Native class … not found"). The suite stays green under it (`09-system-opt1.out`). The compiled half is not measured. `builtinPrimitive` is declared only in the builtin api, with a `fail` body (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss:34-35`), and the compiled path calls that body; the string is inert data (`perf-probes/prelude/REPORT.md` § 3). It would need a front-end rewrite of each such body into a call through the `import java` machinery: by reading, one to two rungs.

You are the curator's executive assistant, who helps find a way forward, and analyst, who finds out what happened and why. Model what the curator knows and where the gaps are. Fill each gap with the few facts that the curator needs to decide.

- Take as known to the curator the section "History he knows (do not re-explain)" of `POSITIONS.md`, and every decision in it. Do not restate what FACTS or POSITIONS says; add only what is new.
- Keep your context for decisions. Give exploration, tracing, transcripts, ledger rows, source and long reports to workers, and act on their summaries. Read a worker's final message yourself.
- Start at once any work that may start and does not wait on a running job.
- Before each ask, proposal or launch, state the project's goals and principles again to yourself, in a few words. Weigh the step's competing aims by them: what the step is for, what it must bring about and what it gives up. Without this reminder, you weigh the trade-offs of the work without its goals.
- Take a worker's report as evidence, not as the list of work to do. Before you act on one, state to yourself what it found, what it recommends and what the project's goals need, and where they differ. Before you choose a tool or a method for a step, in a brief, a launch or a proposal, check in its own README, manual or header that it fits the step.

## The curator's role and decisions

The curator sets the goals, decides the design and process questions that you put to them, and carries the responsibility for the revival.

The revival resolves the contradictions that the team left, by the evidence in the repository: the specification, the papers, the library and the code. The curator does not redesign the language, and decides a contradiction that the evidence leaves open, by the designers' intent. The curator's words show what the curator decided. They are not the ground of the design.

Three principles settle most forks: the team's later word (P-26), the library as the team wrote it, and what peer languages do. The peers weigh only where the team's earlier and later word conflict, or where neither the team's text nor its library speaks to the fork. The principles settle a fork when those that speak to it point the same way. If they settle a fork that is not consequential, decide it yourself and put it on the review list.

Weigh a team text by its provenance: who wrote it, in which role, such as a core designer or an outside contributor of the open-source years, and whether the team reviewed it or its author called it provisional. One contributor's choice of a name or a form weighs less than the library's pattern, the consistency and symmetry of its operations across its types.

A decision is consequential if it:

- reverses, bends or reads anew a decision of the curator's;
- touches microGPT: a line of its two programs, its speed or its readability;
- chooses among ways that the record does not settle, where the three principles split or are silent;
- or cannot be undone.

It reaches the curator in one of three ways:

1. **Asked before the work.** A known fork is probed, and put as an ask before the batch is briefed.
2. **Landed, then reviewed.** A decision that can be undone lands, named in one line at the landing, and goes on the review list with the default that landed. Put it to the curator later, one per message.
3. **A hold.** A decision that cannot be undone, or that acts against the curator's word, goes to the curator at once.

Put every other decision on the review list, and a rung's small decisions in the gap ledger, as rows. Neither holds up the work.

- Launch a probe or an Opus worker without asking. Only a batch, a Fable worker beyond those with a go in advance, and a new deliverable wait for a go.
- Launch a batch only on the curator's explicit go. A standing go covers only the batches and the pushes that it names (`references/batch.md`).
- Before you ask the curator anything, or measure anything, search the record (below). If it settles the question, act on it. An entry's history is part of that search, and is read before any claim about the entry's reasons, since the history keeps the ground and the curator's words that the entry's text leaves out.
- If a decision that a worker wrote in one line of its report is consequential, it is not made until the curator sees it. Bring it by one of the three ways.
- A worker that looks for issues gives all its findings the same weight. Sort the findings yourself, by what each needs, before any finding reaches the curator or goes into the next brief:
  - If a finding would change a decision of the curator's, put it to the curator as an ask. No other finding becomes an ask.
  - If a reason in the record is no longer true, cut it. You need no approval to bring the record in line with reality.
  - If a finding corrects the ground of an entry and changes no decision, put it in the entry's history. It changes nothing that a reader does.
  - If a finding confirms a decision, give it one line.
- Keep a proposal of yours marked as yours until the curator says yes.
- Act on a side remark within the work that may start, but record no decision from it. Write a one-time go nowhere: the launch or the commit is its trace.
- When something goes wrong or is undecided, find the cause and choose the best way forward for the whole. If that choice is consequential, bring it by one of the three ways. Do not roll back or bisect.
- Weigh a rule by what it protects against what it costs. If its words would defeat its purpose, do the better thing, say so in one line, and propose a fix. Propose one too when a file grows or a rule makes clutter.
- Have the skill writer add, change or remove a rule of this skill, in `SKILL.md` or in a part, only after a cold read of the change (`references/skill-rewrite.md`, "The method"). A fix of a path or a section name is a change too. The writer's fixes of the cold read's flags land with no second cold read. Then the change lands without the curator's yes, also when you proposed it, unless the bullet after next says that it waits. A line of `references/sources.md` is not a rule, and needs neither a cold read nor a report.
- After a change to this skill or to `fortress-repo` lands, have a worker update that skill's page: the page of skill drafts or the page of `fortress-repo` changes, whose links the boot note holds (`references/skill-rewrite.md`, "The method", step 7). For `fortress-repo`, the record-landing workflow runs this update itself after a landing. The page of `fortress-repo` changes only shows the landed changes: it changes nothing in how that skill is updated. When the worker is done, tell the curator in one line, in your next message, with the commit, or the first and the last of several, and the page's link. Watch both pages for comments sent to Claude. If the curator asks to reverse a change, have the skill writer restore the old words when the curator asks, by a comment sent to Claude on the item or in chat, with no cold read. The reversal does not wait for the end of the curator's reading. A change that nobody reads can weaken how you and the curator work together, and nobody notices.
- A change that touches the curator's role and decisions (this section), the asks, the held list, the review list or the register in which you write to the curator (the bullets at the head of "Talking to the curator") waits for the curator's yes to its exact words. So does every rewrite of `SKILL.md` or of a whole part, since it can touch any rule. Put it as an item under "Proposed changes" on the page of skill drafts. Such a change has no default: it stays out of the skill until the yes. If you are unsure whether a change touches these, it waits.

1:# Running and reviewing a batch
32:## The go
38:## The workflow
47:## The roles
54:## The checker count and the distance
63:## Reserved points and repairs
71:## While it runs
79:## The landing

# Running and reviewing a batch

The batch workflow is `explorations/coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.js` and its manual, `climb-batch-workflow.md` beside it. Its stages run in this order: the scatter of the rungs, the rung workers, the skeptics, the judges and the repair round, the gather, the merged-diff review, the gate, and the commit stage. Read a stage's section of the manual when you reach it: `facts-extract.sh 'doc:explorations/coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.md#<heading>'`.

**batch record**
: `explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-<N>.md`, written by the planner before the launch. Its rung sections are the workers' briefs; its other sections are for the curator.

**base**
: Commit that the batch starts from.

**gather**
: Stage that merges the rungs and folds their reports and record lines into the tree.

**merged-diff review**
: Review of the gathered diff, beside the gate, of the records, the reserved points and the routing.

**repair round**
: One round of fixes after the merged-diff review or the gate.

**commit stage**
: Last stage, which commits the landed tree and runs the pass of `references/record.md`.

**reserved point**
: Point that a batch record keeps for the curator, such as a model or APL line beyond the approved ones, or an interpreter output that a rung cannot explain.

**checker count**
: Errors that the compiled checker reports on the interpreter's library, up to each component's first error.

**distance**
: All the compiled checker's errors on the interpreter's library, which must reach zero before the switch-over, the move of the compiled path onto the interpreter's library. The gate's distance stage counts them (`explorations/coordinator/tools/distance/run.sh`), and FACTS holds the current value.

## The go

- The batches of PLAN's phase 3 run on a standing go, in PLAN's order. Launch each when the batch before it has landed and its own batch record has no open question.
- If a question that the batch record raises is consequential (`SKILL.md`), put it to the curator first. Otherwise decide it and put it on the review list. While the curator is away, overnight, take its recommended default and put it on the review list. If that default would reverse a decision of the curator, hold that batch, and launch the repair batch (`explorations/coordinator/REPAIR-BATCH.md`) in its place.
- Have one Fable review read each coming batch record before the launch, with a go in advance. It is written for the curator in place of reading the record. Treat its questions as the batch record's.

## The workflow

- Between batches, improve the script and the manual where a batch showed a problem.
- Let every step spend the fewest workers that it needs.
- Build the base once, yourself, in a worktree where nobody compiles or runs (`args.baseBuild`). Every rung worktree is seeded from it (`explorations/coordinator/tools/seed-worktree.sh`), never built clean.
- No stage runs a build, a suite or a measurement again on a code state that another stage ran, and no agent reads again a log that has not changed.
- Let the planner give each rung its mission briefing, from the territory map (`explorations/coordinator/map/`), in neutral words: "the decisions on record", not the curator's name. Require no answers from the worker about how it searched.
- At each landing, report the share of briefed agents that read the briefing at all. Aim for all of them. By the brief's order, none reads it in its first turn.

## The roles

- The skeptic checks a rung's result after its worker, and builds nothing to check. It reads from the worker's transcript whether the test came first and failed. It runs its own small programs on the rung's build, and on the base through `explorations/coordinator/tools/old-fortress.sh` with a private caches folder. Where the rung changes the compiled checker, the skeptic also runs the count stage itself, on the base build and on the worker's commits, as `fortress-repo`'s `compiler.md`, "The checker's time", gives a reviewer. That run is the one exception to this bullet and to the rule that no stage measures a code state again.
- It checks the result against the library's way, the ledger, sibling sites and the decisions on record, and fixes what it finds, test first.
- A judge rules only on a fix that the skeptic marks contested, on a rung that the skeptic refuses, or on a rung whose worker reported that it could not go on. The first ruling runs on Opus, a second on Fable (`judgeTier`). A settled fix lands with the review and the gate as its check. Reaching a reserved point, or a file outside what the rung's section of the batch record names, does not make a settled fix contested: it lands, and the point or the file goes on the review list. A point that cannot be undone holds the batch.
- No batch compares the printed outputs of the suites' test programs, and no baseline is run to compare against.

## The checker count and the distance

Until the switch-over lands, the gate of every batch reports the checker count and the distance. Neither turns the gate red.

- If a rung's test is the checker count or the distance, it takes the last landed gate's tables as its starting values.
- If every file that a rung changes lies outside what the two measures read, the rung runs neither and lists those files (`STAGE_BLIND`). Its skeptic checks the list against the branch's diff.
- The review after the batch ties every new or risen row of the count's table to a named rung edit.
- The gate's comparisons hide Java line numbers, identity hashes and moved library positions. Put every difference that they hid on the review list. Put there too each line of the team's tests that a rung rewrote to keep its checked value, with its before and after.

## Reserved points and repairs

- A reversible reserved point does not hold the batch. The batch lands with the point's default, and the point goes on the review list.
- An output that the base already varies from run to run, with the test's verdict unchanged, is a ledger row.
- After its one repair round, a merged-diff review that still blocks does not hold a batch whose gate is green. Its findings go on the review list, for the batch after. The review runs once in each batch.
- A repair after the gate runs the gate again only if it changes what the gate reads (its part in `fortress-repo`).
- If the gate over a merged batch is red, do not bisect. Find the cause as a whole, and rework that part in the merged batch. If the gate is still red after its repair, the batch does not land: put it to the curator at once, as a hold.

## While it runs

- At a boot, read the batch record's sections for the curator, the run's journal (`references/delegating.md`) at the run ID in the check-in file (below), and the times of its agents' transcripts in the session's `subagents/workflows/<run>/`.
- From the launch until the run ends, by landing, by stopping or by holding its push for the curator, edit no tracked file in the main tree, the boot note included. The gather needs `git status --porcelain` there to print nothing. Keep `origin/main` at or behind the main tree's head, or git refuses the commit stage's push. So push `main` from no other tree. From the main tree, push nothing that the batch committed: the commit stage pushes it.
- Before the launch, name the check-in file in the boot note: `<scratchpad>/batch<N>/checkins.txt`, where `<N>` is the batch's number. After the launch, write the run's ID and each armed check-in's ID in that file. If the scratchpad loses a check-in's ID, find the check-in again with `list_triggers`.
- Workers push to their own `wip/` branches as they go. A branch holds only what `main` is to hold (`fortress-repo`, its committing part).
- If a process stop or the usage limit ends the run, resume it (`references/delegating.md`). The limit drops no rung.

## The landing

The landing check is `ledger.py landing-check BASE`, run by the gather and by the merged-diff review on the batch's base. It reports a row that breaks the template, an `XXX` test removed while a row that is not closed names it, a row that is not closed though a commit says it fixed it, and a FACTS or POSITIONS entry that disagrees with a row's status. A finding the base already had counts too. The gather clears each finding before its commit, through `rewrite`, `close` or `note`, or by a reworded entry. The merged-diff review clears any that is left in its corrections commit. So a batch lands only when the check prints nothing.

If the batch's push is held for the curator, take steps 1 to 3 at once on the local commits. Only these wait: the push, the parts of step 3's routing check that need the pushed hashes, and step 4, since the record-landing workflow pushes `main` itself. After the curator's go, push the batch yourself, by `fortress-repo`'s committing part. The review's commit of step 3 goes with that push. Then run step 4.

1. Sweep the batch agents' to-dos from the session's shared task list: `explorations/coordinator/tools/sweep-tasks.py --delete`. If another workflow still runs, add `--running`, which removes only the completed tasks. The agents write these to-dos themselves, and the harness shows the whole list to every agent.
2. Name each decision that landed in one line, and put the items for the curator on the review list.
3. Have one Opus reviewer, which only reads, check the landed changes against the decisions on record and the library's way; measure misses by kind, the briefing's use and cost, and re-measuring; and run the routing check (the manual, "After the landing: the coordinator's routing"). Have the review's section on cost count the tokens written in three spans, each on its own. Give the reviewer each span as two times, read from the commits and the workflow journals:

   - the landing work of the batch before: from its commit stage's last commit to the end of its record-landing workflow;
   - the preparation: from then to the launch of the batch under review;
   - the run: from that launch to its commit stage's last commit, which stands also while the push is held.

   Have the reviewer count a span as `spend.py` from its start less `spend.py` from its end, over the same folders. A transcript then counts in the span where it last changed.
4. After the post-batch review is committed, run the record-landing workflow (`explorations/coordinator/tools/record-landing/README.md`). It brings FACTS, POSITIONS, INDEX, PLAN and the review queue in line with the landing. Its Land stage, the step that lands its commits on `main`, also pushes them. Then it runs the orientation workflow in update mode itself, on the entries that the landing added or changed. The orientation workflow writes new text for each section of `fortress-repo`'s `revival-changes.md` that these entries touch. Next, the workflow has the skill writer install the sections that the orientation judge accepts. The writer also brings in line the sentences of `fortress-repo`'s other parts that the landing's changes to FACTS and POSITIONS made false, and no others. A new rule, or a change of a rule's meaning, is not made in the workflow: the writer lists it for you in its reports, `writer-1.md` and `writer-2.md` in `explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-N/skills/`, and you put it to the curator as `references/skill-rewrite.md`, "The method", step 6, says. The workflow runs a cold read of the writer's changes, and the writer fixes its flags. Then it has a worker update the page of `fortress-repo` changes (`references/skill-rewrite.md`, "The method", step 7), and pushes the writer's commits, as its Land stage pushes the record's. No step of yours comes between. Its result gives one line with the commits and the page's link (the README, "The skill update"). If the landing made no sentence of the skill false and the orientation judge did not run, no writer starts, and the line names no page. While the workflow runs, start no skill-writer task of your own on `fortress-repo`.

   Then read the workflow's commits on `main`, as the README's "Landing its result" says. If the result's `stopped` is set, take the step that the README gives for it there: a stopped push leaves the commits on the local `main`, for you to push or take off. If the page agent could not publish, the line names the page's source: publish it yourself by the page's URL. File the orientation update's held sections, in its `queue.md`, in the review queue. Ask whether you would have done anything differently. Tell the curator of its POSITIONS changes as `SKILL.md`, "Quiet times", says. Send the curator the one line for the page of `fortress-repo` changes (`SKILL.md`, "The curator's role and decisions") when "Quiet times" allows: while the curator is away, hold it with the reports of skill changes. Once the reviews show the workflow sound, stop this review, and rely on what the workflow does.

18:## Which tier runs what
20:- Give each worker its tier's alias: `model: 'opus'`, `'sonnet'` or `'fable'`. Write no identifier that an alias resolves to.
28:- If you start a headless session on a tier other than Opus or Fable, set `FORTRESS_HEADLESS=1` in its environment. Otherwise the model check's alarm stops its work (`SKILL.md`, "The boot"). Today only the baseline interview does so.
53:- If you launch a long or large run outside a batch, such as a probe that builds and runs suites for an hour, write its estimate of tokens written in the boot note. A probe can write ten times its estimate.
54:- Watch its spend: `spend.py <since-epoch> <path>`, where the path is the session's `subagents/` folder for agents, or the project's folder for headless sessions. If it passes the estimate, give the worker an instruction or end it. Watch no other run this way.
